ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and material counterparties prior to incorporation and continuously thereafter, applying: FATF Recommendations 10, 12, and 24; FINTRAC guidance on politically exposed persons (domestic and foreign PEPs); Global Affairs Canada sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; OFAC SDN list (critical for US-bound Baijiu export payments); and CBSA non-compliant importer/exporter records. Risk tier for ISIC 4632 spirit wholesale is low-to-medium; therefore standard CDD plus PEP and sanctions screening is required prior to bank account opening at any Schedule I Canadian bank.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Government of Alberta, Service Alberta; online filing via authorized service providers) — NUANS name search reports are obtained through the Corporation's registry service provider (https://www.alberta.ca/business-corporations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be in Latin alphanumeric characters and consist of a distinctive element plus a legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.'). Chinese characters are not searchable within the NUANS system; therefore the Chinese Baijiu brand must be transliterated or romanized (e.g., Pinyin) or rendered as an English/registered trademark name (e.g., 'BAIJIU,' 'MOUTAI,' or a coined mark). A parallel Chinese trade name may be used de facto for branding and trademark registration but shall not constitute part of the statutory corporate name unless also expressed in Latin characters.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon NUANS refusal, the applicant may (1) file a written review request with the Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) within 30 days of the refusal, providing evidence of distinctiveness, prior trademark registration, or consent from the objecting party; (2) obtain a no-objection letter from the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission (AGLC) where the rejected token is alcohol-related; (3) resubmit an amended name with a new NUANS report, paying the prevailing name search fee; or (4) appeal to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta by way of judicial review if the Registrar's decision is arbitrary or contrary to the Alberta Business Corporations Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual registered office (via licensed registered agent or law firm) is permitted for corporate registry purposes in Alberta. However, the AGLC liquor license, CBSA exporter records, CRA excise licensing under the Excise Act, 2001, and GST/HST registration require a physical Alberta business address or a licensed bonded warehouse for inventory. The registered office may be a virtual address but cannot be used as the licensed premises for Baijiu storage or handling; a separate commercial premises or third-party warehouse license will be necessary before physical stock flow begins.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: AGLC liquor premises inspection: 100% pre-license inspection and an estimated 20-35% annual probability of unannounced inspection thereafter; CRA/FINTRAC books-and-records audit for first-time exporters: 10-20% within first 12 months; CBSA exporter verification at port of exit: moderate; corporate registered-office physical verification: low (<5%).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, including sections 5-9 on incorporation and articles, sections 102-106 on directors and organizational matters, and applicable regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Alberta Corporate Registry, accessed through an authorized Alberta registry agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation for an Alberta corporation, together with the prescribed Corporate Registry application and registered-office and agent-for-service information.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an Alberta corporation. Shares may be issued for consideration determined by the directors, subject to the Business Corporations Act and the articles. Alberta does not require a statutory escrow account for incorporation capital. Any banking, foreign-exchange, or anti-money-laundering source-of-funds controls remain applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accept and record the subscriptions for the issued shares described in the subscription agreements and issue those shares upon receipt of the agreed consideration. RESOLVED, that the registered office and records office stated in the incorporation filings are adopted as the Corporation’s official addresses, and that the appointed agent for service is confirmed. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve until replacement or resignation. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute incorporation records, and complete all governmental, licensing, tax, and commercial registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Select the Alberta Corporation Name and Confirm Availability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized registry agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Choose either a numbered corporation or a distinctive word name. Obtain the required Alberta name search or NUANS report where applicable, confirm that the name is not confusingly similar or prohibited, and document any foreign-language or translated name separately. No notarization is generally required for standard Canadian incorporation signatures.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-corporation request
Alberta name search or NUANS report, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace the rejected name, obtain an updated search report, correct prohibited wording, and resubmit through the registry agent. A numbered corporation may be used if name clearance is delayed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry filing system operated through an authorized registry agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Articles of Incorporation, including share structure, restrictions on share transfers, number of directors, registered office, records office, and agent for service. Ensure the articles accurately describe wholesale and export distribution of alcoholic beverages without implying unlicensed manufacturing. Submit the signed incorporation package and pay the prescribed Alberta fee in Canadian dollars.
required_dossiers: Name search or NUANS report, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the registry agent's deficiency notice, amend the articles or supporting information, and resubmit. If the name is rejected, file under an approved numbered name or submit a replacement name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry and Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the certificate of incorporation, articles, corporate registry profile, and corporation number. Apply for a Business Number and register the applicable CRA program accounts, including GST/HST and payroll where required. Establish records for beneficial ownership information and maintain the corporation's statutory register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct mismatched corporate data through the registry agent and amend CRA registrations through Business Registration Online or CRA correspondence channels. Preserve all filing confirmations and effective dates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Organizational Governance and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The corporation's board of directors and Alberta Corporate Registry for any required public filing changes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first directors' meeting or execute a written directors' resolution. Adopt the registered and records offices, appoint officers, approve banking authorities, approve the business plan, authorize licensing applications, and issue shares only after receiving legally valid consideration. Record share issuances, transfers, directors, officers, and beneficial owners in the minute book.
required_dossiers: Share certificates or electronic share records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Pass corrective resolutions, cancel and reissue defective share records where legally permitted, amend the minute book, and obtain legal advice before rectifying any unauthorized issuance or director appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Commercial Liquor Business and Determine AGLC Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission, including its liquor licensing and compliance channels.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm whether the proposed activities involve importing, warehousing, wholesaling, agency representation, retail sale, or only export from Canada. Apply for the AGLC liquor licence or authorization applicable to the actual activities and premises. Secure federal excise, Canada Border Services Agency, and destination-market export compliance before shipping. Do not possess, sell, warehouse, or distribute liquor in Alberta without the required authorization.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and corporate profile
Corporate ownership and beneficial ownership information
Background and integrity disclosure forms, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to AGLC requests, correct premises or ownership deficiencies, obtain municipal approvals, and request reconsideration or follow the statutory review or appeal route specified in the applicable licensing decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Clear Municipal, Fire, Building, Occupational Health, and Environmental Requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant Alberta municipality, municipal fire authority, Alberta Occupational Health and Safety, and Alberta Environment and Protected Areas.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain zoning confirmation and a municipal business licence for the warehouse or office. Secure fire inspection approval, confirm building occupancy and structural loading for palletized liquor storage, implement Alberta OHS procedures, and determine whether any environmental approval, registration, or hazardous-material authorization is triggered. Maintain safety data, spill-response, waste, and emergency procedures.
required_dossiers: Fire inspection or fire safety documentation
Warehouse layout and structural load information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct deficiencies identified by the municipality, fire authority, OHS officer, or environmental regulator; obtain revised inspections or approvals; and use the applicable municipal or provincial review and appeal procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission for Alberta liquor activities; Canada Revenue Agency and Canada Border Services Agency for federal excise and import-export controls; municipal authorities for premises approvals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis liquor licence or authorization applicable to the approved activity, premises, and supply-chain role, such as liquor agency, wholesale, warehouse, or other designated class. The exact class must be confirmed with AGLC before operations commence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a project-level full EIA for ordinary liquor wholesale, export, office, and warehouse operations, provided no prescribed industrial activity, major development, release, or regulated waste facility is involved. Site-specific screening is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific wastewater or VOC threshold ordinarily applies to a conventional liquor warehouse with no manufacturing. The operator must prevent releases, manage packaging and hazardous materials lawfully, use authorized waste contractors, and comply with applicable approvals, Alberta release-reporting duties, municipal sewer bylaws, and federal transportation and environmental requirements. Any distilling, blending, bottling, fuel storage, wastewater discharge, or significant hazardous-material activity may trigger additional approvals and quantitative limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal zoning and occupancy approval, fire inspection or fire-safety certification, and any building or development permits. Verify structural floor loading for liquor pallets, aisle and egress compliance, emergency lighting, extinguishers, alarm systems, and storage compatibility. Implement Alberta Occupational Health and Safety requirements, including hazard assessment, worker training, powered-equipment controls, incident reporting, and emergency planning. Obtain additional hazardous-material, transportation, or fire-code approvals where alcohol volumes, storage configuration, or site characteristics require them.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online portal and My Business Account portal; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA on behalf of the Province of Alberta under a single federal-provincial tax administration agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada or making taxable supplies in Canada must obtain a 9-digit Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN). The entity files Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or registers online via Business Registration Online (BRO). Upon approval, CRA issues the BN, a GST/HST program account (RC0001), and a corporate income tax program account (RT0001) where applicable. Non-resident registrants must provide Canadian agent or representative details in prescribed forms and may need to certify treaty residence. The GST/HST account must be obtained before claiming input tax credits or zero-rating exports.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a federally or provincially incorporated corporation is a separate taxable Canadian corporation if incorporated in Canada; for tax purposes it is taxed at the entity level on worldwide income, with territorial limitation for non-resident corporations. Alberta does not recognize check-the-box pass-through classification for corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Canadian income tax law. Corporate tax status follows the legal form of incorporation. Available elections relevant to indirect tax include the streamlined GST/HST election under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act for closely-related corporations to treat supplies as excluded from nil consideration, and annual GST/HST election for filing frequency. For hybrid mismatch purposes, Canadian rules under paragraphs 18(1)(q), 18(1)(r), and 18(1)(t) address disallowed deductions on hybrid arrangements; no elective hybrid regime is available to convert entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST as no provincial sales tax levy exists in the province.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 threshold for the small supplier registration relief; a non-resident making a supply in Canada can be required to register once worldwide taxable supplies from Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter and over the preceding four quarters; registration is mandatory if any single supply or series of supplies for a promotion exceeds CAD 30,000. Voluntary registration is available to recover input tax credits for export-oriented operations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime is in force in Canada. CRA supports Interac e-transfer for tax payments and electronic records, but e-invoicing is voluntary. The CRA launched a voluntary 'E-invoice' registry based on the Peppol network in 2024, but there is no legal mandate for XML invoice clearance or prior CRA approval of invoices. GST return filing must be done electronically for registrants with mandatory electronic filing thresholds, and prescribed information must appear on invoices to substantiate zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 9 of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, a supply of goods made by a supplier is zero-rated if the goods are exported directly by the supplier or delivered by the supplier to a common carrier for export, and evidence of export is held. For a non-resident wholesaler distributing Chinese baijiu from bonded storage, zero-rating applies when the goods are exported from Canada and the supplier maintains documentary proof of export; the supply must be made to a person outside Canada or for use solely outside Canada. Services directly related to export goods (e.g., logistics, storage, freight) may also be zero-rated, but the direct selling and buying of baijiu by an export distributor must satisfy the export evidence rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Customs Export Declaration (via Canada Border Services Agency through the Canadian Export Reporting System, including the AES Export Declaration number and low-value shipment reporting where applicable)
Commercial invoice and purchase contract evidencing the foreign buyer; B/L (Bill of Lading or air waybill) showing exporter, consignee, port of loading, and destination
Inward Remittance Certificate / banking records proving receipt of foreign currency consideration from the Alberta exporter to the Canadian vendor
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA requires exporters to keep prescribed books and records for six years, including export documentation, to substantiate zero-rating of supplies. Absent such proof, the supply is taxable at 5% GST/HST and the registered exporter may be reassessed for all uncollected tax plus arrears interest and penalties. False export claims giving rise to refunds are subject to penalties under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act, including a penalty of CAD 100 plus 25% of the amount wrongly refunded or erroneously sought; knowing misstatements can lead to criminal prosecution. CRA may also claw back input tax credits previously claimed on exported goods and impose no-form-of-relief civil penalties for significant failures under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), established under the Bank of Canada Act (1935), acting with the Department of Finance Canada on exchange-rate policy and with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) on prudential bank supervision. Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange administration agency; the Minister of Finance retains residual intervention powers under the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) that are not exercised in ordinary market conditions. Anti-money-laundering and cross-border funds-flow supervision is performed by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. The Canadian dollar floats freely, and no exchange-control authorization is required for trade settlements, dividend repatriation, loan servicing, or liquidation proceeds. Profit remittance from an Alberta business corporation is unrestricted at the FX level; the operative barriers are fiscal and procedural only: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (25% statutory rate, treaty-reduced to 10% on dividends generally and 5% on qualifying intercorporate dividends where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 10% of the voting shares under Article 10 of the Canada-China DTA (1986)), transfer-pricing documentation under section 247 of the Income Tax Act, thin-capitalization limitations under section 18(4) to 18(8), and CRA information returns (T1134 for foreign affiliates and T1135 Foreign Income Verification Statement where the cost amount of specified foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000). Dividends may be paid in CAD or any freely convertible currency without Bank of Canada approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline on export proceeds. A licensed Alberta exporter may retain foreign currency balances in CAD, USD, CNY, or other acceptable currencies at any Canadian Schedule I bank, may hold funds offshore, and may convert at commercial market rates. The only binding obligations are reporting thresholds, not surrender: all financial institutions must report incoming and outgoing electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, together with large-cash-transaction reports and suspicious-transaction reports, to FINTRAC. The commodity-level licensing controls applicable to liquor export (Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Act permits and the federal Importation of Intoxicating Liquors Act) relate to lawful movement of goods, not to foreign-exchange surrender.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as a supplementary clearing rail and LOW if proposed as the sole treasury infrastructure. Canada does not license offshore digital EMIs as deposit-taking institutions; such entities must register as money services businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC and, where applicable, register as payment service providers under the Retail Payment Activities Act administered by the Bank of Canada (registration framework effective November 2024). International EMIs such as Wise Business, Airwallex, Payoneer and LianLian Global typically classify alcohol distribution as a restricted or higher-risk goods category and apply enhanced review, and their balances are not CDIC-insured. PRC-oriented cross-border payment platforms usually condition service on the merchant holding a Chinese business registration, which does not fit a Canadian-incorporated baijiu exporter. An EMI may be used for low-value FX conversion and supplier payments, but the primary corporate treasury and trade-finance functions must remain with a Schedule I bank that can issue documentary credits and provide regulatory-grade reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly incorporated Alberta corporation with non-resident directors or ultimate beneficial owners, at least one physical appearance by a director or authorized signing officer at a Canadian branch of the principal bank is generally mandatory for first-time onboarding unless a recognized global-client introduction or a qualifying foreign-bank KYC reference is available. Remote onboarding is permitted by some banks under a stricter bundle: notarized and apostilled corporate documents, live video identity verification of every director and UBO, certified passport copies and address verification, a banker's reference letter issued by a PRC financial institution, and a statutory declaration signed by each director. Remote-only opening without a foreign-banked reference is rarely approved for a newly incorporated liquor-vertical company because the PCMLTFA requires that financial institutions take reasonable measures to ascertain identity and that the risk of non-face-to-face business be mitigated with additional documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident PRC ultimate beneficial owner and newly incorporated Alberta company with no Canadian credit history, creating elevated geographical and identity-verification risk in the bank's risk-rating engine.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Alberta Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Status from the Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES); the foreign shareholder's Chinese business license and articles of association; a UBO ownership chart with passport copies and tax residence certificates; board resolution appointing a Canadian-resident signing officer; bank reference letter from the PRC relationship bank; source-of-wealth documentation including bank statements and prior-year audited financial statements of the shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Alcohol distribution classification: internal high-risk-goods flag reflecting duty evasion, smuggling, counterfeit and diversion typologies for spirits wholesale, including high-proof traditional sorghum baijiu.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid AGLC liquor licence or permit under the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Act; federal authorization for international liquor movement under the Importation of Intoxicating Liquors Act; CRA excise duty filing and payment evidence; supply-chain documentation for each shipment (commercial invoices, packing lists, certificates of origin, laboratory certificates of analysis for alcohol content and contaminants); CBSA customs entry records; and a buyer compliance matrix evidencing destination-market licences such as U.S. federal TTB permits and state import authorizations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity and high-value SWIFT flows to and from PRC and Hong Kong counterparties, with same-day transaction aggregation approaching the CAD 10,000 FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer reporting threshold and possible structuring or trade-based money-laundering alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sale and purchase contracts matching the terms of each documentary credit; commercial invoices, packing lists and transport documents (original bill of lading or airway bill); customs entry numbers; MT103 and MT700 records; warehouse receipts and inventory movement reports; a written treasury policy requiring segregated settlement accounts for trade payables; and monthly three-way reconciliation reports reconciling the accounting system, trade documents and bank statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin-capitalization optics and dependency on shareholder loans to fund import purchases; sustained negative retained earnings or intercompany loan reliance can be interpreted as a financial-crime indicator involving hidden debt, layering or round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal share subscription agreement evidencing the paid-in capital injection and corresponding bank debit and credit confirmations; a shareholder loan agreement with arm's-length commercial terms and repayment schedule; a board-approved capitalization plan; 24-month cash-flow forecasts and pro-forma financial statements; documentary proof of the source of transferred funds; and a written remittance policy confirming that upstream profits will be distributed only by declared dividends after bank approval of the return-of-capital or dividend instruction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: the non-resident shareholder executes a SWIFT MT103 payment with complete originator and beneficiary identifiers in fields 50K and 59, and with the narrative in field 70 stating either Share capital contribution and share subscription or Shareholder loan for trade finance. The beneficiary bank credits the designated Capital Escrow Account quoting the Alberta corporate charter number and the board resolution number in the payment narrative. Where the amount is CAD 10,000 or more, the Canadian bank automatically files a FINTRAC electronic-funds-transfer report. If a non-Canadian establishes the business in Canada, an Investment Canada Act notice for a new Canadian business (ISED Form 4) must be filed within 30 days after the establishment of the business. The bank's relationship team requires the corporate share register, directors' resolution authorizing share issuance, the escrow agreement where applicable, and a notarized UBO certification before any funds are released for operations. Capital-injection funds may not be pledged or set off against trade lines unless a separate security agreement is executed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for open-account supplier payments, customs duties, freight, insurance and distribution settlements; every outbound message must carry the entity's BIC, Canadian transit-account routing identifiers, and precise recipient details to avoid sanctions false positives. Documentary rail: commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700 or MT710) issued by the Canadian relationship bank for the import leg from PRC suppliers, governed by UCP 600, preferably confirmed by a Shanghai, Beijing or Hong Kong bank; required presentations include the original bill of lading, insurance certificate, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and quality or quantity certificate. Sales leg: the Alberta entity presents export documents under the buyer's letter of credit, with proceeds settled by MT202 or MT103 cover. Contingent rail: standby letters of credit (MT760) guarantee performance and prepayment obligations. For CNY-denominated legs, the clearing may transit through the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) where the Canadian bank maintains a CNY correspondent relationship, subject to the dealer's CNY settlement balance limits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/CNY, USD/CNY) with maturities of up to 24 months, executed under a standard ISDA or Canadian Master Agreement with a Schedule I bank; no Bank of Canada or OSFI prohibition applies.
Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collar structures for contingent trade flows, purchased from a licensed Canadian financial institution.
FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for multi-currency liquidity and term trade-finance matching, subject to an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA collateral terms.

Offshore CNY non-deliverable forwards (USD/CNH and CAD/CNH) transacted through authorized international banks in Hong Kong or Singapore where onshore CNY liquidity is constrained; speculative NDF positions without an underlying trade exposure are not permissible.
Bank-offered prepayment and performance risk hedges embedded in trade-finance facilities, permitted only where the notional amount is expressly linked to documented import or export exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Business Corporations Act, Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's fiscal year-end anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a statutory late fee (CAD 25); failure to file for 2 consecutive years permits the Registrar to administratively dissolve/strike off the corporation; reinstatement requires additional filings and fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporate Income Tax Return (federal T2 with Alberta provincial schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the sixth month following the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the due date incurs a penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delinquency up to 12 months; continued non-filing may lead to an arbitrary assessment, interest, prosecution, and loss of corporate compliance status with CRA.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit threshold is set by the Alberta Business Corporations Act for a private business corporation. An independent audit is mandatory only if the corporation is a distributing/public corporation, a reporting issuer, or if its Articles or a unanimous shareholder agreement so require; for a private wholesale exporter, audit may be waived by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for Canadian private corporations; IFRS is mandatory for public interest entities or reporting issuers, and may be elected voluntarily or required by shareholders/cross-border financiers.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Alberta BCA, the corporation must maintain and annually verify its register of individuals with significant control (ISC/UBO). Share transfers trigger a mandatory re-examination of the register, which must be updated within 15 days of any such transfer. A formal annual confirmation should be recorded in board or shareholder meeting minutes. Alberta does not yet require a separate provincial UBO registry filing; federal UBO reporting may apply if the corporation is incorporated federally or elects to register with Corporations Canada.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO/ISC Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 – USD 350 per annum for Alberta registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 11,000 per annum for a certified audit, if required or voluntarily obtained by a small/medium private corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No specific statutory tax holidays for liquor export; general incentives include SR&ED tax credits (15-35% on qualifying R&D) and accelerated capital cost allowance for certain assets. Alberta does not impose provincial sales tax, but this does not affect income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T-2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta combined) filed via CRA's e-file (EFILE) or paper; mandatory electronic filing for corporations with gross revenue exceeding CAD 1 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., if fiscal year ends December 31, deadline is June 30 of the following year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from all sources, including export sales of baijiu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income; non-resident corporations with Canadian-source income must file T-2 and report only Canadian-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses, including cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct expenses reasonably allocated to Canadian-source income; maintain contemporaneous documentation for cross-border transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before deductions; apply loss carryforwards and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may claim treaty deductions only if eligible; otherwise, apply Canadian domestic rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal and provincial tax payable after credits (e.g., foreign tax credits, investment tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must compute tax on Canadian-source income; treaty relief may reduce withholding taxes on dividends, interest, and royalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months (max 17%). Repeated failure: 10% plus 2% per month. Daily surcharge for failure to file information returns (e.g., T106) up to CAD 100 per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500. Interest on unpaid tax at prescribed rate (currently 8% for 2025).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends paid to non-residents (unless reduced by treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under the Canada-China Tax Treaty (1986), the non-resident shareholder must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (Form NR301) to the Canadian payer before payment. The payer must complete Form NR601 (or equivalent) and retain the certificate. For dividends, the treaty rate is 15% for portfolio dividends and 10% if the beneficial owner is a company that owns at least 10% of the voting shares. The application must be made to the CRA for a refund if excess withholding was applied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 25% for royalties and 25% for interest (subject to exceptions for arm's-length interest). Treaty rates under Canada-China: 10% for royalties (including industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment) and 10% for interest (with certain exemptions for government or financial institution interest).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if gross revenue exceeds CAD 20 million and cross-border transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1 million (per transaction or aggregate). Master File required if gross revenue exceeds CAD 100 million. Form T106 (Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions) must be filed if total transactions with non-residents exceed CAD 1 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) like the UAE, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and treaty abuse provisions require that transactions have a bona fide business purpose and economic substance. For treaty benefits, the beneficial ownership test and principal purpose test apply. A shell company without real business activities may be denied treaty relief and face penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of export revenue, false deductions, or misrepresentation of transfer pricing to reduce taxable income in Canada.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act, gross negligence penalty of 25% of the understated tax; criminal tax evasion penalties up to 200% of the tax evaded, fines up to CAD 1 million, and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts if they failed to withhold or remit source deductions (e.g., payroll) or if they authorized fraudulent filings. Civil restitution, travel bans, and personal bankruptcy may result.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a conduit with no real business activity, no employees, no physical presence, or no substantive decision-making in Canada, solely to claim treaty benefits or shift profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reassessment of income, and penalties under GAAR (25% of the tax benefit). CRA may also impose a 10% penalty for failure to file T106. In severe cases, criminal charges for conspiracy to defraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for taxes and penalties if they knowingly participated in a sham arrangement. They may face civil restitution, travel restrictions, and imprisonment for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register as a Money Services Business (MSB) or report large cash transactions (over CAD 10,000) to FINTRAC, or failing to implement a compliance program for export payments via wire or letters of credit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative penalties up to CAD 1 million for corporations, and criminal penalties up to CAD 2 million and imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be personally liable for AML violations if they directed, authorized, or acquiesced in the non-compliance. They may face fines, imprisonment, and travel bans.
